newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia to introduce anti-dumping law - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia to introduce anti-dumping law - paper.

text.p: The Serbian government announced anti-dumping measures to protect the country's metal industry, but warned producers they must prepare for international competition, Belgrade dailies reported on Thursday.

"With Yugoslavia joining the World Trade Organisation and other international institutions it will have to liberalise its imports regime," dailies quoted Serbian Industry Minister Oskar Fodor as saying.
"This entails Yugoslavia protecting its own market in the manner applied by countries with a market economy, and that means introducing an anti-dumping law."
No details about the new law were immediately available.
He said the metal industry would have to expect more competitive market conditions inside the country as well as on foreign markets.
Yugoslavia's steel makers have repeatedly called on the government to protect them from dumping practices by Eastern European suppliers.
